translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled as Left Vice Director while keeping his general’s rank, then made Intendant of Danyang with the added title of Regular Cavalier Attendant.

sentences.zh: 蘊以姻戚，不欲在內，苦求外出，復以為都督浙江東五郡、鎮軍將軍、會稽內史，常侍如故。

translations.literal: Yun, as affinal kin, did not wish to be inside; he bitterly sought to go out; again he was made military overseer of the five commanderies east of the Zhe River, Army-securing General, interior secretary of Kuaiji, Regular Cavalier Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: Unwilling to remain at court as an in-law, he begged for a provincial assignment and was named commander of the five eastern Zhe commanderies, Army-securing General, and interior secretary of Kuaiji, still holding his cavalier attendant title.

sentences.zh: 蘊素嗜酒，末年尤甚。

translations.literal: Yun by nature was fond of wine; in late years it was especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun had always loved wine, and drank more heavily in his last years.

sentences.zh: 及在會稽，略少醒日，然猶以和簡為百姓所悅。

translations.literal: When he was in Kuaiji, he had slightly fewer sober days, yet still by mildness and simplicity was pleasing to the hundred surnames.
translations.idiomatic: In Kuaiji he was seldom sober, yet his easy, unpretentious manner kept the people fond of him.

sentences.zh: 時王悅來拜墓，蘊子恭往省之，素相善，遂留十餘日方還。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Yue came to pay respects at the tomb; Yun’s son Gong went to visit him; they were always on good terms; then he stayed over ten days before returning.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Yue came to sweep the family tombs, Wang Yun’s son Wang Gong, an old friend, visited him and stayed more than ten days.

sentences.zh: 蘊問其故，恭曰：「與阿太語，蟬連不得歸。

translations.literal: Yun asked the reason; Gong said: ‘Speaking with A’tai, it linked like cicadas and I could not return.’
translations.idiomatic: Asked why he had stayed so long, Wang Gong said, ‘Conversation with A’tai just went on and on.’

sentences.zh: 」蘊曰：「恐阿太非爾之友。

translations.literal: ’ Yun said: ‘I fear A’tai is not your friend.’
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun said, ‘I doubt A’tai will prove a true friend to you.’

sentences.zh: 」阿太，悅小字也。

translations.literal: ’ A’tai was Yue’s childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: A’tai was Wang Yue’s childhood name.

sentences.zh: 後竟乖初好，時以為知人。

translations.literal: Afterward they indeed deviated from initial friendship; people of the time thought him one who knew men.
translations.idiomatic: The two later fell out, and contemporaries said Wang Yun had read character shrewdly.

sentences.zh: 太元九年卒，年五十五，追贈左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Taiyuan he died, age fifty-five; he was posthumously awarded Left Grand Master of Splendid Carriage, opener of office peer with the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 384 at fifty-five and was posthumously honored as Left Grand Master of Splendid Carriage with Three Dukes’ establishment.

sentences.zh: 長子華，早卒。

translations.literal: His eldest son Hua died early.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Wang Hua died young.

sentences.zh: 次恭，在列傳。

translations.literal: Next Gong is in the arrayed biographies.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Wang Gong has a biography elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 恭弟爽，字季明，強正有志力，歷給事黃門侍郎、侍中。

translations.literal: Gong’s younger brother Shuang, styled Jiming, was forceful and upright with ambition and strength; he passed through Palace Attendant and Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong’s brother Wang Shuang, courtesy name Jiming, was blunt and resolute and served as Palace Attendant at the Yellow Gate and then Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝崩，王國寶夜欲開門入為遺詔，爽距之，曰：「大行晏駕，皇太子未至，敢入者斬！

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu died, Wang Guobao by night wished to open the gate and enter to make a death testament; Shuang barred him, saying: ‘The great traveling carriage has halted; the heir apparent has not arrived—who dares enter shall be beheaded!’
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaowu’s death, Wang Guobao tried to force the palace gates at night to forge a will. Wang Shuang blocked him: ‘The emperor has just died and the crown prince is not here—enter and you die!’

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: ’ Then he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guobao withdrew.

sentences.zh: 爽嘗與會稽王道子飲，道子醉呼爽為小子，爽曰：「亡祖長史與簡文皇帝為布衣之交。

translations.literal: Shuang once drank with Prince of Kuaiji Daozi; Daozi drunk called Shuang ‘boy’; Shuang said: ‘My late grandfather the chief clerk with Emperor Jianwen had common-cloth friendship.’
translations.idiomatic: Once, drinking with Prince Daozi of Kuaiji, the prince drunk called him ‘boy.’ Wang Shuang replied, ‘My late grandfather was sworn friend to Emperor Jianwen when both were commoners.’

sentences.zh: 亡姑、亡姊伉儷二宮，何小子之有！

translations.literal: ’ My late aunt and late elder sister were paired spouses to the two palaces—what ‘boy’ is there!’
translations.idiomatic: My aunt and sister both married into the imperial house—who are you calling “boy”?’

sentences.zh: 」及國寶執權，免爽官。

translations.literal: ’ When Guobao grasped power, he dismissed Shuang from office.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Guobao took power, he cashiered Wang Shuang.

sentences.zh: 后兄恭再起事，並以爽為甯朔將軍，參預軍事。

translations.literal: Afterward elder brother Gong again raised affairs; together they made Shuang Pacifying-the-North General, joining in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Gong, the empress’s brother, rose again, he named Wang Shuang Pacifying-the-North General on his staff.

sentences.zh: 恭敗，被誅。

translations.literal: When Gong was defeated, he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong’s defeat cost Wang Shuang his life.

sentences.zh: 褚爽，字弘茂，小字斯生，恭思皇后父也。

translations.literal: Chu Shuang, styled Hongmao, childhood name Sisheng, was the father of Empress Gongsi.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Shuang, courtesy name Hongmao, called Sisheng in childhood, was the father of Empress Gongsi.

sentences.zh: 祖裒，父歆。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Pou; his father Xin.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Chu Pou; his father Chu Xin.

sentences.zh: 爽少有令稱，謝安甚重之，嘗曰：「若期生不佳，我不復論士矣。

translations.literal: Shuang in youth had a fine reputation; Xie An greatly esteemed him and once said: ‘If Qisheng were not fine, I would no longer discuss gentlemen.’
translations.idiomatic: Praised from youth, he won Xie An’s high regard: ‘If Qisheng were not exceptional, I would give up judging men altogether.’

sentences.zh: 」為義興太守，早卒，以后父，追贈金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: ’ He was Administrator of Yixing, died early; on account of being the empress’s father, he was posthumously awarded Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Administrator of Yixing but died young; as the empress’s father he was posthumously named Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 爽子秀之、炎之、喻之，義熙中，並歷大官。

translations.literal: Shuang’s sons Xiuzhi, Yanzhi, and Yuzhi, in the Yixi period, all passed through great offices.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Chu Xiuzhi, Chu Yanzhi, and Chu Yuzhi all rose to high office under Yixi.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：羊琇托肺腑之親，處多聞之益，遭逢潛躍之際，預參經始之謀，故得繾綣恩私，便蕃任遇。

translations.literal: The historian says: Yang Xiu relied on diaphragm-and-viscera kinship, dwelt in the benefit of much hearing, met the time of lurking and leaping, beforehand joined the planning of founding the enterprise; therefore he obtained lingering favor in private, convenient repeated appointment and encounter.
translations.idiomatic: The historians write: Yang Xiu was the emperor’s intimate kinsman, well placed to learn state secrets; he helped plan the rise of the Jin house and so won deep personal favor and repeated high appointments.

sentences.zh: 憑寵靈而逞欲，恃勢位而驕陵，屢犯憲章，頻干國紀，幸逢寬政，得免刑書。

translations.literal: Relying on favor and numinous power he gave rein to desire; trusting power and position he was arrogant and overbearing; repeatedly he violated statutes, frequently impinged on state norms; luckily he met lenient government and was spared the penal documents.
translations.idiomatic: He abused imperial favor, threw his weight about, broke the law again and again, yet escaped severe punishment only because the throne was indulgent.

sentences.zh: 王愷地即渭陽，家承世祿，曾弗聞於恭儉，但崇縱於奢淫，競爽于季倫，爭先于武子，既塵清論，有斁王猷，雖復議行易名，未足懲惡勸善。

translations.literal: Wang Kai’s territory was none other than Weiyang; his house inherited age’s emolument; he never heard of respectful frugality, only exalted indulgence in extravagance and dissipation; vying in brilliance with Jilun, striving to be first before Wuzi; already he soiled pure discussion, had flaw in kingly plans; though again they debated conduct and changed his name, it was not enough to punish evil and encourage good.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kai, kin by marriage to the throne and heir to hereditary stipends, scorned frugality; he tried to outshine Shi Chong in display and to outdo Wang Ji in extravagance, fouling public opinion and the royal model. A harsher posthumous name could hardly punish vice or teach virtue.

sentences.zh: 弘理儀形外朗，季野神鑒內融，仲祖溫潤風流，幼道清虛寡欲，皆擅名江表，見重當時，豈惟后族之英華，抑亦搢紳之令望者也。

translations.literal: Hongli’s bearing and form outwardly bright, Yeye’s spirit mirror inwardly fused, Zhongzu warm and moist, elegant bearing, Youdao clear and empty, few desires—all monopolized fame south of the Yangzi, were esteemed in their time—how could they be only the empress clan’s flower; they were also the girdled sash’s fine repute.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yi’s looks were open and bright; Chu Pou read men with inward clarity; Wang Meng moved with gentle grace; He Chong (styled in the text as Youdao) lived spare and detached—all were luminaries south of the Yangzi and pillars of their age, ornaments not only to the imperial in-laws but to the whole gentry.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：托屬丹掖，承輝紫宸。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: Entrusting connection to the crimson flank, inheriting radiance from the purple palace.
translations.idiomatic: Eulogy: Tied to the crimson harem, they borrow luster from the purple throne hall.

sentences.zh: 地既權寵，任惟執鈞。

translations.literal: Their territory being power and favor, their charge is only holding the steelyard beam.
translations.idiomatic: Favor makes them mighty; their posts are meant to steady the state.

sentences.zh: 約乃寡失，驕則陵人。

translations.literal: Restraint then has few faults; arrogance then treads on others.
translations.idiomatic: Restraint brings few errors; pride tramples others.

sentences.zh: 覆車遺戒，諒足書紳。

translations.literal: The overturned cart’s left warning—truly enough to write on the girdle sash.
translations.idiomatic: The lesson of the wrecked cart is worth wearing on one’s sash.
